questions.passage: Walter Gropius was a well-known architect, <u>ⓐ widely</u> regarded as one of the pioneers of modernist architecture. However, even this expert architect was once <u>ⓑ troubled</u> when designing an amusement park. He finished most of the main structures except for the pathways between the attractions. Gropius wanted to find the best design for the pathways but could not come up <u>ⓒ with</u> anything that satisfied him. One day, Gropius took a trip to France. The place he went to was famous for its vineyards. Farmers <u>ⓓ were selling</u> grapes along the road near each vineyard. Then, one far ahead <u>ⓔ catching</u> his eye because there was no one selling grapes but only a box by the side of the road.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] Then, one far ahead caught his eye because there was no one selling grapes but only a box by the side of the road. [해석] 그때, 저 멀리 앞에 있는 한 곳이 그의 눈길을 끌었는데, 포도를 파는 사람이 아무도 없고 길가에 상자만 놓여 있었기 때문이다. catching → caught: 주어 'one far ahead'의 주절 동사 자리에 정형동사(과거시제 caught)가 필요합니다.
det.correct: ⓐ widely: 과거분사 regarded를 수식하는 부사 → widely regarded(널리 인정받는) ✅ ⓑ troubled: be troubled(고민하다), was와 결합한 수동태 ✅ ⓒ with: come up with(~을 생각해 내다) 고정 구동사 ✅ ⓓ were selling: 과거진행형, 그 시점 진행 중인 상황 ✅ ⓔ catching: 주어 one far ahead의 주절 동사 자리 → 현재분사는 정형동사 불가 → caught 필요 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 분사(v-ing / p.p.) vs 정형동사: 주어 뒤 동사 자리에는 반드시 정형동사(시제 동사)를 써야 합니다. catch one's eye = ~의 눈길을 끌다 (≈ attract one's attention ↔ go unnoticed)

questions.passage: It turned out that the elderly couple who owned the vineyard were in poor health and could not pick the grapes themselves. Instead, they let people pick as many grapes as they wanted as long as they put five francs in the box. The couple not only (A) <u>[prevented / preventing]</u> their grapes from becoming too ripe by permitting grape picking, but they also provided an enjoyable experience for their customers. Astonished by the elderly couple's idea of (B) <u>[allowing / allowed]</u> customers to freely pick grapes, Gropius thought it would be good to extend this idea to the amusement park design and allow visitors (C) <u>[create / to create]</u> their own paths.
questions.stem: 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] The couple not only prevented ... the idea of allowing ... allow visitors to create [해석] 그 부부는 포도가 너무 익는 것을 막았을 뿐만 아니라 고객에게 즐거운 경험도 제공했다. 고객이 자유롭게 포도를 따게 한 아이디어에 놀란 Gropius는 방문객들이 스스로 길을 만들게 하면 좋겠다고 생각했다.
det.correct: (A) prevented: not only A but also B에서 also provided와 병렬 → 과거시제 동사 prevented ✅ / preventing은 동사 역할 불가 ❌ (B) allowing: 전치사 of 뒤에 동명사 → the idea of allowing ✅ / allowed는 전치사 목적어 불가 ❌ (C) to create: allow + O + to-v 구문 → allow visitors to create ✅ / create(원형부정사)는 allow와 쓰지 않음 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 (A) not only A but also B: 병렬 구조 → prevented ... provided (B) 전치사 + 동명사: the idea of v-ing (C) allow + O + to-v. 비교: let/make/have + O + 동사원형. allow·permit·enable 등은 to부정사를 취합니다.

questions.passage: Employees of the elevator company conducted a customer survey in order to find out why the passengers were so unhappy. The results of the questionnaire <u>ⓐ showed</u> that it was the elevator's slow speed that was causing dissatisfaction. The trip from one floor to the next took nearly fifteen seconds. The employees also discovered that passengers thought the elevator was much <u>ⓑ slower</u> than it actually was because passengers had nothing to do. During the slow ride, some passengers complained and said they felt <u>ⓒ trapping</u>. Even though the employees identified speed as the main source of dissatisfaction, it was not something <u>ⓓ that</u> could be improved immediately due to technological limitations.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] some passengers complained and said they felt trapped. [해석] 일부 승객들은 불만을 토로하며 갇힌 느낌이라고 말했다. trapping → trapped: feel + 보어에서 주어(passengers)가 갇히는 대상이므로 수동의 과거분사 trapped가 필요합니다.
det.correct: ⓐ showed: 주어 The results(복수)의 과거시제 동사, that절 목적어 ✅ ⓑ slower: much + 비교급 + than 구문 ✅ ⓒ trapping: feel + 보어에서 주어가 갇히는 대상 → 수동(trapped) 필요 ❌ ⓓ that: 선행사 something을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 feel + 감정 분사: 주어가 감정을 느끼는 대상이면 p.p. → feel trapped/excited/bored. something/anything/nothing + 관계대명사 that 선호.

questions.passage: In places where people repeatedly walked, small footpaths started to form on the grass. The shapes of the paths were not (A) <u>[unified / diversified]</u>, with some wide and some narrow, because they were formed naturally by visitors. The following year, Gropius used the grass pathways as an outline on which he built (B) <u>[permanent / temporary]</u> pathways, resulting in the most convenient and efficient routes. This pathway design was later chosen as the best road design at the 1971 International Landscape Architecture Symposium in London. It was (C) <u>[contrary / similar]</u> to common sense to allow people to walk on newly sprouted grass because it could damage the grass.
questions.stem: 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] The shapes of the paths were not unified ... he built permanent pathways ... It was contrary to common sense [해석] 길의 모양은 통일되지 않았다. 영구적인 산책로를 만들었다. 상식에 반하는 것이었다.
det.correct: ① unified - permanent - contrary: 길 모양 not unified(통일되지 않은) + 영구적 산책로 + 상식에 반함 ✅ ② diversified: not diversified = 다양하지 않은 → 문맥 불일치 ❌ ③ temporary: 영구 건설 내용에 불일치 ❌ ④ 둘 다 불일치 ❌ ⑤ similar: 역발상 맥락에 불일치 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 unified(통일된) ≈ standardized ↔ diversified(다양화된). permanent(영구적) ↔ temporary(임시의). contrary to(~에 반하는) ↔ similar to(~와 유사한).

questions.passage: Then, one day, one employee of the elevator company began to look at the problem from a different perspective. She thought about it from a passenger's point of view. She thought that what mattered was not speed but ① <u>discomfort</u> and boredom. She asked herself what could be done in this case. After many days of searching for a solution, she proposed installing a mirror inside the elevator. She believed that it could make the elevator appear ② <u>larger</u>, reducing the feeling of being trapped. Also, she believed that people could relieve boredom by looking in the mirror. On a survey done after the mirror was installed, passengers commented on how much ③ <u>faster</u> the new elevator was, even though the speed was exactly the same. Passengers stopped paying attention to the speed of the elevator because they were ④ <u>distracted</u> by looking in the mirror. If the employee had thought only of ways to ⑤ <u>decrease</u> the speed of the elevator to resolve the problem, it might not have been possible to find a solution.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] If the employee had thought only of ways to increase the speed of the elevator [해석] 만약 그 직원이 엘리베이터의 속도를 높이는 방법만 생각했다면 해결책을 찾지 못했을 수도 있다. decrease → increase: 느린 속도가 불만 원인이므로 속도를 '높이는(increase)' 방법이 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.correct: ① discomfort: 중요한 것이 불편함과 지루함 → 적절 ✅ ② larger: 거울로 더 넓어 보이게 → 적절 ✅ ③ faster: 거울 설치 후 더 빨라졌다고 느낌(실제 동일) → 적절 ✅ ④ distracted: 거울로 주의 분산 → 적절 ✅ ⑤ decrease: 느린 속도 해결 = 속도를 높여야 함 → decrease(줄이다) 부적절 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 increase(증가) ↔ decrease(감소). 가정법 과거완료: If + had p.p., might/could/would + have p.p. distracted(주의가 분산된) ≈ diverted ↔ focused.

questions.passage: For example, there was a fast-food company that was concerned about public criticism on ① <u>negative</u> health effects due to the high fat content of fast food. Instead of trying to dispute the public criticism and claim their food was healthy, the company tried something different. They ② <u>discouraged</u> customers from eating fast food, like hamburgers, too often. Unexpectedly, this approach had an interesting effect. The company gained a ③ <u>positive</u> image as being socially responsible, attracting more customers. This approach was also ④ <u>successful</u> in the world of fashion. There was a rising concern about buying clothes and throwing them away quickly. This type of fast fashion trend has a ⑤ <u>constructive</u> impact on the environment because excessive production of clothes produces a massive amount of waste.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] This type of fast fashion trend has a destructive impact on the environment [해석] 이런 패스트 패션 트렌드는 환경에 파괴적인 영향을 미친다. constructive → destructive: 과도한 생산 → 폐기물이라는 부정적 맥락.
det.correct: ① negative: 부정적 건강 영향 → 적절 ✅ ② discouraged: 소비 억제 권유 → 적절 ✅ ③ positive: 긍정적 이미지 획득 → 적절 ✅ ④ successful: 패션계에서도 성공적 → 적절 ✅ ⑤ constructive: 환경에 해로운 맥락에서 '건설적인'은 부적절 → destructive ❌
det.tip: 🔑 destructive(파괴적인) ≈ damaging, harmful ↔ constructive(건설적인). discourage A from v-ing ↔ encourage A to-v.

questions.passage: As we go through life, we may become stuck in a routine, missing out on extraordinary ideas or solutions. In such a situation, we can try considering things from a different angle. By doing so, we can expand our understanding of the world, challenge our assumptions, and find creative solutions to problems. Let's look at two stories that demonstrate the power of thinking differently. In solving problems that are new to us, it is quite easy to get stuck in a particular point of view. However, even a simple shift in perspective can result in a creative solution. So, the next time you face a problem, try thinking about it from a different angle.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] we can try considering things from a different angle ... even a simple shift in perspective can result in a creative solution [해석] 다른 각도에서 사물을 바라보려 시도할 수 있다. 단순한 관점의 변화도 창의적 해결책을 낳을 수 있다.
det.correct: ① 루틴 유지의 중요성: 루틴에 갇히면 안 된다는 내용 ❌ ② 관점 전환을 통한 창의적 문제 해결: 도입·결론 모두 perspective shift → creative solution 강조 ✅ ③ 건축 설계에서 전문가 의견: Gropius 사례는 소재일 뿐 ❌ ④ 기술 혁신: 주제 아님 ❌ ⑤ 비판적 사고 vs 논리적 분석: 언급 없음 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 주제 파악: 도입부+결론부 반복 키워드 → different angle, shift in perspective, thinking differently. perspective(관점) ≈ viewpoint, standpoint.

ch: 관점의 전환을 통한 창의적 문제 해결

questions.passage: Astonished by the elderly couple's idea of allowing customers to freely pick grapes, Gropius thought it would be good to extend this idea to the amusement park design and allow visitors to create their own paths. Upon returning to his project, he instructed the construction team to plant grass in areas where he wanted to create the pathways. When the grass started to grow, he opened the amusement park earlier than planned. In places where people repeatedly walked, small footpaths started to form on the grass. The following year, Gropius used the grass pathways as an outline on which he built permanent pathways, resulting in the most convenient and efficient routes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] allow visitors to create their own paths ... resulting in the most convenient and efficient routes [해석] 방문객들이 스스로 길을 만들게 했고, 가장 편리하고 효율적인 경로가 되었다.
det.correct: ① 잔디 관리: 산책로 설계가 핵심 ❌ ② 사용자가 만든 길, 최고의 설계: 방문객 경로 → 최고의 설계상 수상 ✅ ③ 경제적 효율성: 언급 없음 ❌ ④ 전통적 건축 재해석: 역발상이지 전통 재해석 아님 ❌ ⑤ 농업 혁신: 포도원은 영감의 소재 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 제목 유형: 핵심 소재+메시지를 담은 선지 선택. outline(윤곽) ≈ framework, blueprint.

ch: 사용자가 만든 길, 최고의 설계가 되다

questions.passage: Surprisingly, one fashion company started to persuade people not to buy their clothes. They argued that people should consume less and far more slowly. This unconventional marketing strategy not only raised awareness about the harmful effects of fast fashion on the environment, but also increased the company's sales. People thought that this brand really cared about the environment, and they started to buy more of this company's products. To sum up, both of these companies positioned themselves as responsible brands by discouraging consumption, which ultimately captured the attention and appreciation of a growing audience.
questions.stem: 다음 글이 시사하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] This unconventional marketing strategy not only raised awareness ... but also increased the company's sales. ... positioned themselves as responsible brands by discouraging consumption [해석] 비관습적 마케팅 전략은 인식을 높이고 매출도 증가시켰다.
det.correct: ① 생산량 감소 의무: 핵심은 역발상 전략의 효과 ❌ ② 역발상 → 신뢰+매출 상승: unconventional strategy → increased sales + appreciation ✅ ③ 가격 경쟁력: 언급 없음 ❌ ④ 소비자가 항상 사회적 책임 우선시: '항상'은 과잉 일반화 ❌ ⑤ 패스트 패션 규제: 규제 주장 아님 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 unconventional(비관습적) ≈ unorthodox ↔ conventional. position oneself as = ~로 자리매김하다. '소비 억제 → 신뢰 → 매출 증가'의 역설적 인과관계가 핵심.

ch: 기업은 환경보호를 위해 생산량을 줄여야 한다.
역발상적 접근이 오히려 소비자의 신뢰와 매출을 높일 수 있다.
마케팅에서 가격 경쟁력이 가장 중요한 요소이다.
소비자는 항상 기업의 사회적 책임을 우선시한다.
패스트 패션 산업은 반드시 규제되어야 한다.

questions.passage: Walter Gropius was a well-known architect, widely regarded as one of the pioneers of modernist architecture. However, even this expert architect was once troubled when designing an amusement park. He finished most of the main structures except for the pathways between the attractions. One day, Gropius took a trip to France. The place he went to was famous for its vineyards. It turned out that the elderly couple who owned the vineyard were in poor health and could not pick the grapes themselves. Instead, they let people pick as many grapes as they wanted as long as they put five francs in the box.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] The place he went to was famous for its vineyards. [해석] 그가 간 장소는 포도원으로 유명했다.
det.correct: ① 주요 구조물 설계 어려움: 주요 구조물은 완성, 산책로에 어려움 ❌ ② 프랑스 장소가 포도원으로 유명: famous for its vineyards 일치 ✅ ③ 건강이 좋아서 직접 수확: in poor health → 건강 좋지 않음 ❌ ④ 무료로 딸 수 있었다: 5프랑 필요 ❌ ⑤ 직접 팔기 위해 서 있었다: 건강 문제로 직접 못 팜 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 except for(~을 제외하고): 주요 구조물은 완성 → 산책로만 미완. in poor health(건강 좋지 않은) ↔ in good health.

ch: Gropius는 놀이공원의 주요 구조물 설계에 어려움을 겪었다.
Gropius가 방문한 프랑스의 장소는 포도원으로 유명했다.
노부부는 건강이 좋아서 직접 포도를 수확하였다.
사람들은 포도를 무료로 딸 수 있었다.
노부부는 포도를 직접 팔기 위해 길가에 서 있었다.

questions.passage: Have you ever wondered why there are mirrors in elevators? The world's first successful passenger elevator was installed in a five-story building in New York in 1857. This prominent development brought excitement to the field of architecture by making it possible to build much taller buildings than ever before. Nevertheless, passengers were highly dissatisfied regardless of how practical it was. The results of the questionnaire showed that it was the elevator's slow speed that was causing dissatisfaction. The trip from one floor to the next took nearly fifteen seconds. The employees also discovered that passengers thought the elevator was much slower than it actually was because passengers had nothing to do.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] passengers were highly dissatisfied regardless of how practical it was [해석] 승객들은 아무리 실용적이어도 매우 불만족했다.
det.correct: ① 뉴욕 설치: installed in New York in 1857 → 일치 ✅ ② 더 높은 건물 가능: making it possible to build much taller buildings → 일치 ✅ ③ 실용성에 만족: highly dissatisfied → 불만족 → 불일치 ❌ ④ 약 15초: nearly fifteen seconds → 일치 ✅ ⑤ 할 일 없어서 더 느리게 느낌: passengers had nothing to do → 일치 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 regardless of(~에 상관없이): 양보 의미. dissatisfied(불만족한) ≈ displeased ↔ satisfied. prominent(두드러진) ≈ notable, remarkable.

ch: 세계 최초의 성공적인 승객용 엘리베이터는 뉴욕에 설치되었다.
엘리베이터의 발명은 더 높은 건물 건축을 가능하게 했다.
한 층에서 다음 층까지 이동하는 데 약 15초가 걸렸다.
승객들은 할 일이 없어서 엘리베이터가 실제보다 더 느리다고 느꼈다.

questions.passage: It was contrary to common sense to allow people to walk on newly sprouted grass because it could damage the grass. Moreover, it was unprecedented for an architect to let people do the designing. Nonetheless, Gropius gained insight into creating ideal pathways by _______________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] Gropius gained insight into creating ideal pathways by thinking outside the box. [해석] Gropius는 틀에서 벗어나 생각함으로써 이상적인 산책로 통찰력을 얻었다.

det.tip: 🔑 think outside the box = 고정관념 탈피 ≈ think creatively. contrary to ↔ in accordance with. unprecedented(전례 없는) ≈ groundbreaking.

det.ref: [원문] the employee found the solution by speeding up the customers' perception of time. [해석] 그 직원은 고객의 시간 인식 속도를 높임으로써 해결책을 찾았다.

det.tip: 🔑 perception(인식): 실제(reality)와 대비. speed up ≈ accelerate ↔ slow down. 물리적 속도가 아닌 심리적 체감 시간 변화가 핵심.

questions.passage:
When Not Selling Becomes the Best Sell

Have you ever come across an advertisement that actually encourages customers not to buy a product? It does not seem to make sense, but there are instances where companies have successfully used this somewhat odd approach. For example, there was a fast-food company that discouraged customers from eating fast food too often. Unexpectedly, the company gained a positive image as being socially responsible, attracting more customers.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 "When Not Selling Becomes the Best Sell"이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] When Not Selling Becomes the Best Sell [해석] 팔지 않는 것이 최고의 판매가 될 때. 소비 억제 마케팅이 오히려 이미지와 매출을 높인다는 역설적 내용.
det.correct: ① 재고 관리: 글 내용과 무관 ❌ ② 소비 억제 → 최고의 판매 전략: Not Selling → Best Sell의 역설적 관계 정확 ✅ ③ 온/오프라인 비교: 없음 ❌ ④ 고객 서비스 강화: 소비 억제가 핵심 ❌ ⑤ 할인 행사: 관련 없음 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 함축 의미: 비유적·역설적 의미 파악. Not Selling = 소비 억제 전략. come across ≈ encounter. socially responsible(사회적으로 책임감 있는).

ch: 판매를 중단하면 재고 관리가 효율적이 된다.
소비를 억제하는 전략이 오히려 최고의 판매 전략이 될 수 있다.
온라인 판매가 오프라인 판매보다 항상 효과적이다.
고객 서비스를 강화하면 자연스럽게 매출이 오른다.
할인 행사를 하지 않는 것이 브랜드 가치를 높인다.

questions.passage:
[주어진 글] Then, one day, one employee of the elevator company began to look at the problem from a different perspective. She thought about it from a passenger's point of view.

(A) On a survey done after the mirror was installed, passengers commented on how much faster the new elevator was, even though the speed was exactly the same.
(B) She thought that what mattered was not speed but discomfort and boredom. After many days of searching for a solution, she proposed installing a mirror inside the elevator.
(C) She believed that it could make the elevator appear larger, reducing the feeling of being trapped. Also, she believed that people could relieve boredom by looking in the mirror.
questions.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [해석] 주어진 글: 한 직원이 다른 관점에서 문제를 바라봄. (B) 중요한 것은 불편함과 지루함 → 거울 설치 제안. (C) 거울의 기대효과. (A) 설치 후 결과.
det.correct: ① (A)-(B)-(C): 결과가 원인보다 먼저 ❌ ② (A)-(C)-(B): 순서 부적절 ❌ ③ (B)-(C)-(A): 생각→기대효과→결과의 자연스러운 시간순 ✅ ④ (B)-(A)-(C): 기대효과(C)가 결과(A) 뒤 ❌ ⑤ (C)-(A)-(B): 주어진 글과 (C) 연결 부자연스러움 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 순서 배열: ① 대명사 연결(She → employee) ② 시간 흐름(생각→제안→효과→결과) ③ 논리적 인과. (B)의 She thought that...이 주어진 글과 자연스럽게 이어집니다.

questions.passage: ① Upon returning to his project, Gropius instructed the construction team to plant grass in areas where he wanted to create the pathways. ② When the grass started to grow, he opened the amusement park earlier than planned. ③ The amusement park featured a variety of rides imported from several European countries. ④ In places where people repeatedly walked, small footpaths started to form on the grass. ⑤ The following year, Gropius used the grass pathways as an outline on which he built permanent pathways, resulting in the most convenient and efficient routes.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장을 고르시오.

det.ref: [해석] ③ 놀이공원에는 유럽 여러 나라에서 수입한 다양한 놀이기구가 있었다. → 산책로 설계 과정과 무관한 놀이기구 정보.
det.correct: ① 잔디 심기 지시: 산책로 설계 첫 단계 ✅ ② 일찍 개장: 산책로 형성 위한 조치 ✅ ③ 유럽 수입 놀이기구: 산책로 주제와 무관 ❌ ④ 오솔길 형성: 자연적 산책로 과정 ✅ ⑤ 영구 산책로 건설: 설계 마무리 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 무관 문장: 글의 중심 화제에서 벗어난 문장을 찾으세요. 화제 = 산책로 설계 과정. ③은 놀이기구(rides)로 주제 이탈. feature = ~을 갖추고 있다.

questions.passage: It turned out that the elderly couple who owned the vineyard were in poor health and could not pick the grapes themselves. Instead, they(ⓐ) let people pick as many grapes as they(ⓑ) wanted as long as they(ⓒ) put five francs in the box. The couple not only prevented their grapes from becoming too ripe by permitting grape picking, but they(ⓓ) also provided an enjoyable experience for their customers.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 they가 모두 같은 대상이면 T, 다른 대상이 있으면 F를 고르시오.

det.ref: [해석] ⓐ they = 노부부: let의 행위 주체. ⓑ they = 사람들(people): 포도를 원하는 주체. ⓒ they = 사람들: 돈을 넣는 주체. ⓓ they = 노부부: The couple과 동일. ⓑ·ⓒ는 노부부가 아닌 people을 가리킵니다.
det.correct: ⓐ they = the elderly couple(노부부): let의 행위 주체 ✅ ⓑ they = people(사람들): as many as they wanted → 원하는 주체 = 포도 따는 사람들 ⓒ they = people(사람들): they put five francs → 돈 넣는 주체 = 사람들 ⓓ they = the elderly couple: The couple과 동일한 주어 ✅ → F(다른 대상이 있음)
det.tip: 🔑 지칭 추론: 동사의 행위자/대상으로 판단. '원하는 만큼 딴다(they wanted)' = 사람들. '5프랑을 넣는다(they put)' = 사람들. as long as = ~하는 한 (조건).

questions.passage: It was contrary to common sense to allow people to walk on newly sprouted grass because it could damage the grass. Moreover, it was unprecedented for an architect to let people do the designing. Nonetheless, Gropius gained insight into creating ideal pathways by thinking outside the box.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

[조건] (A), (B) 각각 한 단어로 쓸 것

[요약문] Gropius gained (A) into creating ideal pathways by thinking outside the (B).

det.ref: [원문] Gropius gained insight into creating ideal pathways by thinking outside the box. [해석] Gropius는 틀에서 벗어나 생각함으로써 이상적인 산책로 통찰력을 얻었다.
det.correct: (A) insight: gain insight into ~(~에 대한 통찰력을 얻다)의 핵심 명사. (B) box: think outside the box(고정관념을 벗어나 생각하다)의 관용 표현.
det.tip: 🔑 gain insight into = ~에 대한 통찰력을 얻다 (insight ≈ understanding). think outside the box = 고정관념 탈피 ≈ think creatively.

questions.passage: Even though the employees identified speed as the main source of dissatisfaction, it was not something that could be improved immediately due to technological limitations.
questions.stem:
다음 <보기>의 단어를 활용하여 우리말을 영어로 옮기시오.

[조건] 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하되, 필요시 어형을 변환할 것. 한 문장으로 쓸 것.

[보기] it, possible, not, improve, immediately, due to, technological, limitation

[우리말] 기술적 한계 때문에 그것은 즉시 개선될 수 있는 것이 아니었다.

det.ref: [원문] it was not something that could be improved immediately due to technological limitations [해석] 기술적 한계 때문에 그것은 즉시 개선될 수 있는 것이 아니었다. improve → be improved(수동태), limitation → limitations(복수형).
det.correct: 핵심 문법: ① it was not something that could be improved: 관계대명사 that 수식. ② could be improved: 조동사 + 수동태. ③ due to technological limitations: due to + 명사(원인). ④ limitation → limitations(복수형 변환).
det.tip: 🔑 due to + 명사 = ~ 때문에 (≈ because of). could be improved: 조동사+수동태. limitation(한계) ≈ restriction, constraint.

questions.passage: The couple not only prevented their grapes from becoming too ripe by permitting grape picking, but they also provided an enjoyable experience for their customers.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 형태를 쓰시오.

The couple not only prevented their grapes from ( become ) too ripe by permitting grape picking, but they also provided an enjoyable experience for their customers.

det.ref: [원문] prevented their grapes from becoming too ripe [해석] 포도가 너무 익는 것을 막았다. prevent A from v-ing 구문에서 전치사 from 뒤에 동명사 필요. become → becoming.
det.correct: prevent A from v-ing 구문: 전치사 from의 목적어 자리 → 동명사 becoming 정답. become(원형)이나 to become(to부정사)은 불가.
det.tip: 🔑 prevent/stop/keep/prohibit + A + from + v-ing: A가 ~하는 것을 막다. 전치사 from 뒤 반드시 동명사. 비교: enable/allow/permit + A + to-v.
